newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Savage shuts Clarksville zinc roaster.
newsitem.headline: Savage shuts Clarksville zinc roaster.

text.p: Savage Resources Ltd said on Thursday it had shut down the roaster/acid plant at its Clarksville zinc refinery in Tennessee ahead of a maintainence programme scheduled for October.
"Anticipation of robust zinc prices for the next two or three years heavily influenced the timing of this shutdown," the company said.

"To further assure the reliability of the plant, this opportunity is being used to undertake extra maintenance works (costing about A$1 million) as part of the shutdown including substantial rebricking in the roaster, boiler maintenance and an up-grade of piping in the acid plant," Savage said.
The company said the roaster and boiler refractories and some of the boiler tubes which would be replaced were originally installed 19 years ago.
The roaster/acid plant is scheduled to come on line again by the end of April.
A build-up of stockpiled calcine and the purchase of third party zinc metal at attractive prices has enabled metal production and sales to continue, Savage said.
"The cost of this long life maintenance work, the buildup of calcine stocks and associated costs is estimated to be approximately US$5 million," it said.
The Clarksville plant produces about 105,000 tonnes of zinc a year.
